subject: Chemistry
title: Biomolecules (Chemistry)
summary: Carbohydrates are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones: monosaccharides (glucose, fructose), disaccharides (sucrose, maltose, lactose) and polysaccharides (starch, cellulose, glycogen).
Glucose exists mainly in a six-membered ring (pyranose) form with α and β anomers. Sugars with a free aldehyde or ketone group are reducing sugars; sucrose is non-reducing.
Proteins are polymers of α-amino acids joined by peptide bonds. Their structure has four levels (primary to quaternary); denaturation destroys the higher levels but not the primary structure.
Nucleic acids (DNA, RNA) are polymers of nucleotides — sugar + base + phosphate. Vitamins and hormones are small molecules with big biological roles.

formulas.name: Glucose structure evidence
formulas.formula: HI → n-hexane (straight chain);  acetylation → pentaacetate (5 –OH);  HCN → cyanohydrin and NH₂OH → oxime (C=O);  Br₂ water → gluconic acid (–CHO);  HNO₃ → saccharic acid (–CHO and 1° –OH)

formulas.name: Evidence against open chain
formulas.formula: no Schiff's test and no reaction with NaHSO₃;  pentaacetate does not react with NH₂OH;  two anomers (α, β)
formulas.when: Why glucose has a ring structure.

formulas.name: Anomers and mutarotation
formulas.when: Change of specific rotation in solution.
formulas.mistake: Anomers differ only at C1; they are not mirror images.

formulas.name: Disaccharides and their links
formulas.formula: sucrose = α-glucose (C1) + β-fructose (C2), non-reducing;  maltose = α-glucose C1–C4, reducing;  lactose = β-galactose C1–C4 glucose, reducing

formulas.name: Invert sugar
formulas.formula: sucrose (+66.5°) + H₂O → glucose (+52.5°) + fructose (−92.4°) → mixture is laevorotatory
formulas.when: Why hydrolysed sucrose is called invert sugar.

formulas.name: Polysaccharides
formulas.formula: starch = amylose (15–20%, unbranched, α-1,4) + amylopectin (80–85%, branched, α-1,6 at branches);  cellulose = β-1,4 glucose;  glycogen = highly branched, like amylopectin
formulas.when: Structure of storage and structural carbohydrates.

formulas.name: Peptide bond
formulas.formula: –CO–NH–, formed by condensation of –COOH of one amino acid and –NH₂ of the next; n amino acids → n − 1 peptide bonds

formulas.name: Zwitterion
formulas.formula: H₃N⁺–CHR–COO⁻; at the isoelectric point the net charge is zero
formulas.when: Why amino acids have high melting points and are water-soluble.

formulas.name: Levels of protein structure
formulas.formula: primary (sequence) → secondary (α-helix, β-pleated sheet; H-bonds) → tertiary (overall folding: H-bonds, disulphide, ionic, van der Waals) → quaternary (subunits)

formulas.name: Nucleotide
formulas.formula: nucleoside (base + pentose sugar) + phosphate;  nucleotides joined by 3′–5′ phosphodiester bonds

formulas.name: Bases
formulas.formula: DNA: A, G, C, T;  RNA: A, G, C, U;  purines A, G;  pyrimidines C, T, U;  pairs A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds)

formulas.name: Vitamins and deficiencies
formulas.formula: fat-soluble A, D, E, K;  water-soluble B group and C.  A → night blindness;  B₁ → beri-beri;  B₁₂ → pernicious anaemia;  C → scurvy;  D → rickets;  K → delayed blood clotting
formulas.note: B₁₂ is water-soluble but can be stored in the liver.

examples.title: Peptide bonds
examples.problem: How many peptide bonds are in a hexapeptide?

examples.title: Number of tripeptides
examples.problem: How many different tripeptides can be made from glycine, alanine and valine if each may be used more than once?

examples.title: Reducing sugar?
examples.problem: Which are reducing: glucose, fructose, sucrose, maltose, lactose?
examples.solution: All except sucrose. In sucrose both anomeric carbons (C1 of glucose and C2 of fructose) are used in the glycosidic bond, so there is no free hemiacetal group.

examples.title: Denaturation
examples.problem: What happens when an egg is boiled?
examples.solution: Heat denatures albumin: the secondary and tertiary structures unfold and the globular protein coagulates. The primary structure (amino acid sequence) is unchanged.

examples.title: Essential amino acids
examples.problem: Name the difference between essential and non-essential amino acids.
examples.solution: Essential ones (valine, leucine, isoleucine, lysine, threonine, methionine, phenylalanine, tryptophan, histidine, arginine) must come from food; non-essential ones (glycine, alanine, glutamic acid) are made in the body.

examples.title: DNA vs RNA
examples.problem: Give three differences between DNA and RNA.
examples.solution: DNA has deoxyribose, thymine and a double helix; RNA has ribose, uracil and is usually single-stranded. DNA carries genetic information; RNA (m, t, r) helps make proteins.

topics.title: Classification of carbohydrates
topics.explain: Reducing vs non-reducing; aldoses vs ketoses; monosaccharides (cannot be hydrolysed), oligosaccharides (2–10 units) and polysaccharides. D/L refers to the configuration at the last chiral carbon relative to glyceraldehyde, not the direction of rotation.

topics.title: Fructose
topics.explain: A ketohexose, laevorotatory; it forms a five-membered (furanose) ring. It reduces Tollens' and Fehling's reagents because in alkaline medium it isomerises to an aldose.

topics.title: Amino acids
topics.explain: α-Amino acids have –NH₂ and –COOH on the same carbon. Acidic (aspartic, glutamic), basic (lysine, arginine) and neutral types. All except glycine are optically active and mostly have the L-configuration.

topics.title: Fibrous and globular proteins
topics.explain: Fibrous proteins (keratin, myosin) are long, thread-like and insoluble; globular proteins (insulin, albumin) are spherical and water-soluble.

topics.title: Enzymes
topics.explain: Biological catalysts, mostly globular proteins, highly specific; they lower activation energy. Example: maltase converts maltose to glucose.

topics.title: Hormones
topics.explain: Chemical messengers from endocrine glands: steroid (oestrogen, testosterone), polypeptide (insulin, glucagon) and amino-acid derivatives (thyroxine, adrenaline). Insulin lowers and glucagon raises blood glucose.

topics.title: Biological functions of nucleic acids
topics.explain: DNA replicates itself and carries heredity; transcription makes mRNA, and translation on ribosomes (with tRNA carrying amino acids) makes proteins.
